overview: CICC is one of China's leading investment banks, founded in 1995 as the country's first Sino-foreign joint-venture securities firm (original partners included the former China Construction Bank and Morgan Stanley) and now majority state-controlled through Central Huijin Investment. It offers a full-service platform spanning investment banking, equities, FICC, asset management, private equity and wealth management, with dual listings on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (A-shares, 601995) and Hong Kong Stock Exchange (H-shares, 3908.HK) and an extensive cross-border network (Hong Kong, New York, London, Singapore, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Vietnam, Dubai). The company is in the final stages of a transformative merger by absorption of Dongxing Securities and Cinda Securities, which will roughly double its asset base and move it from roughly 12th to around 4th among Chinese brokerages by assets.

business_model.summary: CICC earns fee/commission income (investment banking underwriting and advisory, brokerage commissions, asset management fees, wealth management/advisory fees), net interest income (margin financing, securities-backed lending, treasury), and investment income (proprietary trading and investment gains on its own securities/derivatives book). Revenue is a mix of transactional (brokerage, underwriting), recurring fee-based (AUM-linked asset/wealth management fees) and market-sensitive trading income, making overall revenue highly correlated with capital-market turnover and sentiment. H1 2026 total revenue was RMB26.4bn, up 43.7% YoY, with fee and commission income 41.4%, interest income 20.2%, and investment income 38.4% of the total.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B/B2C: large domestic and multinational corporates, central/local SOEs, sovereign and government issuers, ~15,600 global institutional investors (QFII, NSSF, mutual funds, insurers), plus a growing retail/HNW wealth management client base (~11 million clients, RMB5.39 trillion in client assets as of H1 2026)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Mainland China (A-share and onshore bond underwriting, onshore brokerage and wealth management) with a significant and growing Hong Kong/offshore franchise (H-share IPOs, offshore bonds, cross-border M&A, Stock Connect); overseas offices in Hong Kong, New York, London, Singapore, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Vietnam and Dubai support cross-border business

competitive_position.market_position: Historically a top-tier but mid-sized player (~12th by assets pre-merger) with a disproportionately strong franchise in high-end investment banking, cross-border M&A, QFII/institutional equities and offshore bond underwriting; the pending Dongxing/Cinda absorption is expected to vault it to roughly 4th by total assets and into the top 3-5 by revenue, among China's largest brokerages alongside CITIC and Guotai Haitong

moat_factors.description: 30-year history, founded with Morgan Stanley's involvement, widely regarded as China's most prestigious investment bank for large-cap IPOs and cross-border deals; research team ranked #1 China research by Asiamoney/Extel for multiple consecutive years

Central Huijin (PBoC-linked sovereign entity) is controlling shareholder, giving CICC privileged access to sovereign, SOE and policy-driven mandates (Belt and Road, Panda bonds, SOE restructuring) and a strong hand in regulator-sponsored industry consolidation

Longstanding first-mover advantage in offshore IPOs, offshore bond issuance, and cross-border M&A for Chinese issuers; ranked #1 in global IPOs for PRC-based companies and #1 in Hong Kong IPO sponsorship/bookrunning in H1 2026
QFII market share #1 for 23 consecutive years; deep relationships with NSSF, insurers, mutual funds and large corporates create switching costs and repeat mandates

Absorbing Dongxing and Cinda materially increases balance sheet, branch network and capital base, improving ability to compete for large capital-intensive mandates and prime brokerage/market-making business

weaknesses: Historically smaller balance sheet/net capital than CITIC and the merged Guotai Haitong, limiting capacity for capital-intensive business (margin lending, market-making, underwriting risk) pre-merger
Revenue heavily levered to China/Hong Kong capital market turnover and sentiment — highly cyclical, with investment income particularly volatile

Integration risk and execution complexity absorbing two separate full-license brokerages (Dongxing, Cinda) simultaneously, including technology, culture, and overlapping branch/license rationalization
Wealth management and retail brokerage franchise (mainly via CICC Wealth Management, formerly China Investment Securities) is less differentiated than top-tier retail-focused peers
Regulatory/geopolitical sensitivity given state ownership and the strategic nature of the securities industry

growth_drivers: Completion and integration of the Dongxing Securities / Cinda Securities merger by absorption (share-swap ratios of 0.4376 CICC A-shares per Dongxing A-share and 0.5210 per Cinda A-share), roughly doubling total assets to ~RMB1 trillion and lifting CICC from ~12th to ~4th largest Chinese broker by assets, with management targeting a '1+2>3' synergy outcome across business capabilities, network coverage, client resources and capital

Regulatory tailwind: CSRC policy explicitly favors consolidation into ~10 leading securities firms, with 2-3 globally competitive investment banks targeted by 2035 — positions scaled, state-backed players like CICC favorably
Record capital markets activity in China/Hong Kong in H1 2026 (A-share average daily turnover +97% YoY, HK IPO proceeds +93% YoY) driving brokerage, IPO underwriting, and margin financing volumes
Continued #1 ranking in global IPOs for PRC-based companies and in the onshore/offshore M&A market, supporting investment banking fee growth as China's IPO and M&A markets recover

Wealth management transformation from product sales to buy-side fee-based advisory (AUM of advisory services >RMB170bn, product AUM >RMB530bn, both at record highs), diversifying toward more recurring revenue

Growth in asset management and private equity AUM (total group AUM RMB1.81 trillion as of H1 2026, +4% HoH) including REITs origination leadership and government-backed funds (e.g., RMB50bn Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Venture Capital Guiding Fund)
RMB internationalization and 'Belt and Road' cross-border financing (Panda bonds for sovereigns including Pakistan and Kazakhstan, offshore RMB bonds) expanding CICC's international franchise

AI-related investment banking demand (sci-tech/STAR Market reforms welcoming unprofitable AI companies) and AI-enabled internal productivity tools (client-facing and advisor agents) in wealth management

business.risk: Revenue cyclicality tied to capital markets
business.description: Brokerage, underwriting and trading income move directly with market turnover, IPO volumes and index levels; a market downturn (as seen in prior years) can sharply cut revenue and profit, as shown by the swing from RMB37.4bn revenue in 2022 to softer years before the 2025-2026 rebound

Simultaneously absorbing two separately licensed, listed securities firms (Dongxing, Cinda) entails operational, IT, cultural and personnel integration risk, dissenting-shareholder cash-option mechanics, and potential disruption to day-to-day operations during the transition

business.risk: Competitive intensity from mega-mergers among peers
business.description: Rival consolidation (e.g., Guotai Junan/Haitong forming a larger entity that displaced CITIC as largest by assets) means CICC must execute its own deal well to keep pace; smaller/mid-tier brokers are also consolidating (Soochow/Donghai, Orient/Shanghai Securities)
Franchise strength skews toward large-cap IPOs and SOE/sovereign mandates; more volatile or smaller-ticket business lines are less differentiated

financial.description: Gearing ratio of 82.3% as of H1 2026 (up from 80.9% at FY2025) and operating leverage ratio of 6.0x; substantial reliance on wholesale funding (REPOs, debt securities issued, interbank placements) exposes the company to funding-market stress
Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss and derivatives totaled RMB394.7bn (39.6% of total assets) as of H1 2026 — mark-to-market volatility can swing reported profit materially

H1 2026 net cash from operating activities fell 84.4% YoY to RMB1.47bn due to growth in FVTPL financial instruments and margin-client receivables, illustrating working-capital sensitivity to balance sheet growth

regulatory.risk: CSRC/SSE approval and completion risk for the merger
regulatory.description: While the SSE's M&A Review Committee approved the restructuring (August 27, 2026) and CSRC formally accepted applications (September 7, 2026 per press reports), final regulatory sign-off, share-exchange mechanics, and delisting of Dongxing/Cinda A-shares must still be completed without incident

Securities companies operate under strict net capital, risk coverage, liquidity coverage and leverage regulatory ratios; risk coverage ratio declined from 183.0% (FY2025) to 168.5% (H1 2026) and capital leverage ratio from 12.2% to 10.4%, approaching closer to regulatory thresholds as the balance sheet scales up
As a Central Huijin-controlled entity, CICC's strategy and capital actions (dividends, M&A) are subject to alignment with state objectives, which can cut both ways for minority H-shareholders

macro.description: Management explicitly cites 'mounting spillover risks from geopolitical conflicts' and global energy/market shocks; GDP growth of 4.7% YoY in H1 2026 was achieved amid a 'complex and volatile external environment'

Hang Seng Index, Hang Seng China Enterprises Index and Hang Seng TECH Index fell 10.7%, 15.2% and 18.9% respectively in H1 2026 even as mainland A-share indices rallied, showing a potential decoupling risk for CICC's HK-listed H-shares and HK-based business lines

US IPO/follow-on activity for PRC-based companies collapsed in H1 2026 (US IPO proceeds -93.8% YoY), reflecting ongoing US-listing friction that could structurally shift business toward HK/A-share venues

execution.description: Combining management teams, risk-control systems, and client relationships across three previously independent, separately regulated brokerages while maintaining the 'all staff, whole process, full coverage' unified risk control culture CICC emphasizes as a core strength

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese securities industry in a structural consolidation phase actively encouraged by the CSRC, which aims for roughly 10 leading securities firms and 2-3 globally competitive investment banks by 2035; 2025-2026 saw a wave of state-directed mega-mergers (Guotai Junan/Haitong, CICC/Dongxing/Cinda, Soochow/Donghai, Orient/Shanghai Securities) reshaping the competitive landscape. Near-term industry fundamentals are strong: H1 2026 average daily A-share turnover rose ~97% YoY, margin financing balances hit record highs (>RMB3 trillion), and HK IPO proceeds rose ~93% YoY.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — brokerage, underwriting, and trading/investment income are all strongly correlated with equity market turnover, IPO windows, and investor sentiment; asset/wealth management fees are comparatively more stable (AUM-linked) but still market-sensitive
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — PBoC's accommodative monetary policy supports margin financing demand and lowers funding costs for CICC's wholesale liabilities (REPOs, debt securities); a tightening cycle would raise funding costs and could dampen market turnover
key_input_costs: Compensation/headcount costs (talent competition for bankers and research analysts)
Cost of wholesale funding (REPO rates, bond coupons)
Regulatory capital requirements driving need for capital raises

recent_developments.event: SSE's M&A and Restructuring Review Committee approved the Dongxing/Cinda merger by absorption as compliant with restructuring conditions (August 27, 2026); CSRC formally accepted/approved administrative applications in early September 2026 covering the merger and related changes in substantial/controlling shareholders of Dongxing and Cinda subsidiaries

Press reports indicate A-shares of CICC, Dongxing Securities and Cinda Securities were slated for suspension from September 15, 2026 ahead of merger completion, with Dongxing and Cinda expected to voluntarily delist from the SSE; deal valued at an estimated RMB113.85 billion, the largest A-share securities-sector M&A to date

Total assets grew 27.4% in just six months (RMB782.8bn at FY2025 to RMB997.1bn at H1 2026) on organic balance-sheet expansion amid record capital-market turnover, not merger consolidation — Dongxing and Cinda were NOT yet consolidated at 30 June 2026, as the restructuring was still pending SSE/CSRC approval at that date (approved Aug/Sep 2026, after period end). Non-controlling interests rose materially in H1 2026 (from ~RMB2.3bn to ~RMB8.3bn), but per the H1 2026 equity statement this was almost entirely (~RMB6.0bn) CICC Wealth Management perpetual bonds being reclassified/booked as non-controlling interests, plus a ~RMB98m minor contribution — unrelated to the Dongxing/Cinda merger

Record first-half results: total revenue and other income of RMB26.0bn (+39.2% YoY), profit attributable to shareholders of RMB8.2bn (+89.3% YoY), EPS of RMB1.621 (+99.1% YoY), weighted average ROE of 7.6% (vs 4.2% in H1 2025)
Preliminary Q1 2026 results beat expectations: profit attributable to shareholders of RMB3.58bn, up 75.2% YoY (CASs basis), driving Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan to reiterate bullish ratings

Analyst price target increases: JPMorgan raised target to HK$28.5 (Overweight) from HK$24.5, citing expected ROE improvement from 9.4% (2025) to 11.3% (2027) aided by post-consolidation leverage; Goldman Sachs reiterated Buy with HK$28.15 target (~11x 2027 P/E)

FY2025 results: total revenue and other income RMB40.8bn (+22.9% YoY), profit attributable to shareholders RMB9.79bn (+71.9% YoY), weighted avg ROE 9.4% (vs 5.5% in 2024), total assets RMB782.8bn (+16.0% YoY); proposed FY2025 full-year dividend of RMB3.20 per 10 shares (tax inclusive)
CICC, Dongxing Securities and Cinda Securities announced a trading halt to plan the major asset restructuring/merger, with a preliminary share-swap agreement signed shortly after

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (August 2026) and 2025 Annual Report

items.target: Consolidate leadership in large A-share and Hong Kong IPOs, focus on 'new quality productive forces' and sci-tech enterprises, broaden full life-cycle coverage
items.notes: No specific numeric revenue/EPS guidance disclosed; qualitative strategic priorities reiterated each period

items.target: Expand REITs AUM and long-term stable management fee income; grow mutual fund and advisory AUM
items.notes: Group AUM reached RMB1.81 trillion at H1 2026 (+4% vs FY2025); CICC Fund Management AUM +7.9% HoH to RMB294.8bn

items.target: Continue shift to advisory-based (buy-side) model; grow advisory AUM beyond RMB170bn and product AUM beyond RMB530bn
items.notes: Both metrics described as reaching new historical highs in H1 2026

items.target: Complete merger by absorption of Dongxing Securities and Cinda Securities; capture '1+2>3' synergies across business capabilities, network, clients and capital
items.notes: SSE review committee approval obtained Aug 27, 2026; CSRC administrative approval process advancing as of Sept 2026 per press reports; no proposed 2026 interim dividend yet pending completion of restructuring

items.metric: ROE trajectory (analyst estimate, not company guidance)
items.notes: JPMorgan estimate citing favorable market environment and post-consolidation operating leverage; not formal company guidance

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman and President emphasized CICC's 30th anniversary, the strategic goal of becoming a 'world-class investment bank' under the new 15th Five-Year Plan, and explicit pursuit of M&A to accelerate growth: 'we vigorously promote the merging with Dongxing Securities and Cinda Securities by way of merger by absorption. We strive to fully unleash the complementary advantages in business capabilities, network coverage, client resources, and financial capital, to achieve the effect of 1+2>3.' Management has not issued a specific 2026 interim or full-year dividend plan, stating the board will consider profit distribution 'upon completion of the Proposed Mergers.'

bull_case: Transformative, regulator-blessed merger with Dongxing and Cinda roughly doubles CICC's asset base and propels it into the top tier (~4th largest) of Chinese brokerages, with management and sell-side analysts expecting meaningful ROE accretion (9.4% in 2025 toward 11%+ by 2027) from scale and operating leverage

Best-in-class brand and franchise in high-value investment banking (global IPOs for PRC companies, PRC M&A #1 ranking, Hong Kong IPO leadership) positions CICC to capture a disproportionate share of a recovering China/HK new-issue and M&A market

State ownership via Central Huijin provides policy tailwinds, privileged access to SOE/sovereign mandates, and alignment with Beijing's explicit strategy of consolidating the industry into a handful of globally competitive investment banks

H1 2026 results show strong operating momentum (revenue +39%, profit +89%, ROE +3.4pp) driven by record capital market turnover, with wealth management's shift to fee-based advisory and growing AUM adding a more recurring revenue layer

Positive sell-side sentiment with both Goldman Sachs (Buy, HK$28.15 PT) and JPMorgan (Overweight, HK$28.5 PT, raised from HK$24.5) reiterating bullish views tied to the merger and the improving market backdrop
bear_case: Revenue and profit are highly cyclical and dependent on continued strong China/Hong Kong equity market turnover and IPO activity; a market correction (already visible in H1 2026 Hang Seng weakness, down 10.7-18.9% across indices) could quickly reverse recent gains

Integration of two separately licensed, listed securities firms (Dongxing and Cinda) simultaneously carries meaningful execution risk — technology, risk-control, culture and personnel integration could disrupt operations or delay promised synergies

Rising balance-sheet leverage (gearing ratio 82.3%, operating leverage 6.0x as of H1 2026) and declining risk-coverage/capital-leverage ratios increase financial risk as the post-merger balance sheet scales, with heavy reliance on wholesale funding (REPOs, debt issuance)

Intensifying consolidation among peers (Guotai Junan/Haitong merger creating a larger rival, other mid-tier tie-ups) means the competitive bar keeps rising; failure to execute as well as rivals could leave CICC relatively disadvantaged despite its own merger

US-China capital markets friction continues to compress the US-listing channel for PRC companies (US IPO proceeds -93.8% YoY in H1 2026), and the dividend plan remains on hold pending merger completion, creating near-term capital-return uncertainty for H-shareholders
